name: Proxmox_VE_Cluster_Backups
description: Backup jobs, the guests each one covers, each guest's last backup and failed backups, and the guests no backup job covers.
technicalNotes:
BatchScript. One instance per guest per backup job, grouped by job (the job's comment, or its id when it has none), plus one instance per guest that no job covers, in the group "No backup job". A guest in two jobs has an instance under each. Needs only the PVEAuditor role.

The last backup and failures come from the logs of vzdump backup runs, read newest first; reading stops once every job guest has a successful backup, normally after the newest run. Backup files on a storage are not read: Proxmox hides them from a read-only token.

Calls per run, of discovery and collection alike: /cluster/backup, one included_volumes call per job, /cluster/backup-info/not-backed-up, one task-list call per online node, one log read per backup run read (normally one), and /cluster/resources once when a failed all or pool run must be matched to its guests. None grows with guest count. At most the newest 50 runs are read, so a guest whose last good backup is older than that reads as having none.

LastBackupAgeHours warns after 8 days (192 hours) and raises an error after 14 (336): a backstop that catches a daily or weekly job that has stopped -- disabled, its storage offline, or failing before it reaches the guest -- without knowing its schedule. Tighten it per job group, for example > 26 on a daily job; raise it on a job that runs less often than weekly. A guest with no good backup in the newest 50 runs has no age, so it does not alert. LastBackupSizeGB is the archive size the run logged; Proxmox Backup Server runs log none, so it stays empty there.

FailedSinceLastBackup is 1 when a run newer than the guest's last good backup, to the same storage, failed for the guest: its log names the guest as failed, or the run failed (a status other than OK or WARNINGS) before reaching it. Such a run names no guest in its log, so its guests are the VMIDs on its command line, or for an all or pool job the job's guests on the run's node. One that fails before its job starts logs no command line: its guest is the task id's VMID and its storage the one its error names; naming neither, it fails no guest. If any online node's backup runs cannot be read, these three datapoints stay empty rather than guess.

The alert names the guest, its job and the failure: the description reads "Backed up by <job>. Last failure in the run started <time> on <node>: <reason>", the reason being the log's own ("CT is locked (backup)") or the run's status, and the alerts print it (##DSIDESCRIPTION##). Only discovery can write a description, so it runs every 15 minutes, reads the same runs as collection, and stamps the failed run's start in auto.pve_backup_failed_at; FailedSinceLastBackup reads 1 once that stamp names the failure, and is withheld until then, so the alert opens with its reason, normally within 15 minutes. A failure whose run ended more than an hour ago alerts without waiting. The time is in the Collector's time zone.

IncludedVolumes and ExcludedVolumes count the guest's volumes the job backs up and leaves out; the instance properties auto.pve_backup_included_volumes and auto.pve_backup_excluded_volumes name them, the excluded ones with Proxmox's reason ("not a volume" for a bind mount). A bind mount is never in a Proxmox backup, so ExcludedVolumes ships without a threshold.

NotCovered ships without a threshold: guests are often left out of backups on purpose. Set > 0 on the "No backup job" group where every guest must be covered.

Applies on the cluster role: resources whose pve.cluster.role is active or standby, which the NetScan sets. Only one of the pair collects -- the active resource, or the standby while the active one is down or has lost quorum. The other prints nothing, so its datapoints read No Data and the pair never alerts twice. The suite has no addCategory_* PropertySource: the NetScan sets the categories and pve.cluster.role, and the product page lists them for a resource added by hand.

Units: LastBackupSizeGB in GB, LastBackupAgeHours in hours. MB and GB are decimal (10^6 and 10^9 bytes); the product page states the suite's convention.

datapoints.name: NotCovered
datapoints.description: 1 for a guest that no backup job covers, 0 for a guest in a job. Ships without a threshold; see technical notes.

datapoints.name: JobEnabled
datapoints.description: 1 when the backup job is enabled.

datapoints.name: IncludedVolumes
datapoints.description: Volumes of this guest that the job backs up. Their names are in the instance property auto.pve_backup_included_volumes.

datapoints.name: ExcludedVolumes
datapoints.description: Volumes of this guest that the job leaves out, such as bind mounts or disks set to backup=no. Their names and the reason are in auto.pve_backup_excluded_volumes. Ships without a threshold; see technical notes.

datapoints.name: HoursUntilNextRun
datapoints.description: Hours until the job's next scheduled run. Empty when Proxmox reports no next run, such as for a disabled job.

datapoints.name: LastBackupAgeHours
datapoints.description: Hours since the guest's newest successful backup to the job's storage. Warns after 8 days, errors after 14; see technical notes. Empty when none is found in the newest 50 runs.
datapoints.alertBody:
##INSTANCE## has had no good backup for ##VALUE## hours, longer than a daily or weekly schedule allows. The job may be disabled, its storage offline, or its runs failing before they reach this guest.

##DSIDESCRIPTION##.

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.

datapoints.name: LastBackupSizeGB
datapoints.description: Archive size of the guest's newest successful backup, in GB, as the run logged it. Empty for Proxmox Backup Server.

datapoints.name: FailedSinceLastBackup
datapoints.description: 1 when a backup of this guest has failed since its newest good backup. The instance description names the failed run's time, node and reason.
datapoints.alertBody:
A backup of ##INSTANCE## has failed since its last good backup, so the newest copy available to restore is older than the job's schedule promises.

##DSIDESCRIPTION##.

The run's full log is in that node's Task History in the Proxmox web interface.

Status: ##ALERTVALUEDISPLAYSTATUSNAME## (##VALUE##).

This started at ##START##, ##DURATION## ago.
